design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 0 of cd_maturity_withdrawals_and_renewals (Piedmont Crescent Bank, certificates of deposit).

STEP 0. DRAW AND SCOPE.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/regional_retail_bank/tasks/cd_maturity_withdrawals_and_renewals --tasks 2 printed:
  {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
So this task is a tree of two problems, one of them a prerequisite, and its two computations carry 5 and 4
declared factors. The root problem cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty takes 5, the prerequisite problem
cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate takes 4.
Nothing was occupied before this task. This task claims the pair (cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate,
cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty) with the tools record_term_renewal_3666596b and
confirm_partial_withdrawal_44cc2957, that is the base subjects cd_renew and cd_withdrawal. Task 1 is left the
whole of cd_penalty and cd_deposit — the entry a withdrawal already taken still owes and the
restoring add-on deposit that is sized from what the term has lost — which is an independent, load-bearing
tree of its own with its own tools, so the remaining headroom is real and not a leftover.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST.
The caller asks one thing: take as much as possible out of my certificate without closing it. Nothing in what
he says points at the real work. The certificate matured on 2026-05-28 and its grace window closed on
2026-06-07, yet at frozen time 2026-06-12 it still stands in grace_period with the term dates and the rate of
a term that is over. An agent who simply computes a penalty from what the row says charges it at 4.22 percent
on a term that no longer exists and writes 779.11 instead of 687.42. The published rule for the withdrawal
says outright that the penalty is worked out only after the certificate carries the rate and the term dates of
the term running on the day the principal leaves, so the agent must read that sentence, look at the records,
see that the certificate carries no such term, work out from the renewal policy that a term that reached the
end of its grace window is carried into a new one, record that renewal first, and only then compute the
penalty on the certificate as it then stands. Both numbers are then multi-factor reconciliations over a year
of ledger, a checking deposit window, a money market balance and a card ledger: nothing here can be guessed
from a tool list.

DIFFICULTY IN DEPTH AND BREADTH.
Depth: surface goal (cash out of the certificate without closing it) -> the penalty policy's own prerequisite
sentence -> the record shows no running term -> the renewal policy's rate, itself a four-factor computation ->
the certificate now carries 4.14 and a term from 2026-05-28 -> the penalty's charged rate, days, basis, share
and rounding -> the owner's own confirmation. The order cannot be swapped: computing the penalty first fixes
it on the ended term's 4.22 rate and on renewal_count 0, which changes both the charged rate and the share
charged.
Breadth: the renewal rate reads the certificate's own ledger (the 6500.00 deposit posted after maturity), the
checking tier and its deposit count over three months, the money market balance, and twelve months of card
purchases. The penalty reads the certificate's interest credits inside the one month counted back from
today, its earlier
partial withdrawals, the checking tier and opening date, the checking balance, the card tier and its purchase
count over three months, and the money market balance again. Remove any one of them and the number moves — the
factor card below gives the figure each one would otherwise produce.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty (the caller's own request).
Prerequisite problem: cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate.
Edge cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty <- cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate
  kind: value_input. gate: the compute binding applied_rate.
  form: state.
  prerequisite sentence (policy_source, verbatim in the blocked policy's own rule): "The penalty on principal
  taken out of a certificate before maturity is worked out only after the certificate carries the rate and the
  term dates of the term running on the day the principal leaves."
  Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result (the penalty
  on principal taken out before maturity) to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible
  state — the rate, the term start date and the maturity date standing on the certificate — and no action,
  performer or tool is named; (3) no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token, no row id appears in it;
  (4) it is written exactly as hard as the edge is: "only after", no wider (it does not demand anything of
  other certificates) and no narrower.
  Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate's action
  writes a term start date, a maturity date and a rate onto a certificate; the other three policies of the
  difficulty write ledger entries and never touch the term the certificate carries. Derivation: the sentence
  says the penalty waits on the certificate carrying the rate and dates of the term running today; the records
  show maturity_date 2026-05-28 and status grace_period at 2026-06-12, so what it carries is the term that
  ended; the renewal policy's own rule says a term that has reached the end of its grace window is carried
  into a new term whatever the day the bank comes to record it, and that the new term's rate and dates are
  written then — so the one action that can bring the waited-on state about is that renewal. One reading only.
  Unresolved at frozen time: initial_state.cd_certificates.<certificate>.status = grace_period and
  .maturity_date = 2026-05-28, which is fifteen days before frozen_time and five days past the close of the
  ten-day grace window; the row carries term_start_date 2025-05-28 and interest_rate 4.22, the figures of the
  term that ended. Flips to true when the renewal is recorded: status active, term_start_date 2026-05-28,
  maturity_date 2027-05-28, interest_rate 4.14, renewal_count 1.
  Load-bearing (Step 5 run): skipping the renewal and replaying everything else leaves the penalty at 779.11
  instead of 687.42 — the charged rate falls back to 4.22 - 0.15 = 4.07 and the share charged falls from nine
  tenths to the whole figure because renewal_count is still 0.
Resolution order: cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate, then cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty. There are no
parallel edges, so no reordering is possible and order_uniqueness is settled by the single edge itself.
The caller never mentions the prerequisite: user_scenario contains no renewal, no rollover, no term change and
no hint that anything must be sorted out first; he says only that the certificate "came due at the end of May"
as his own timeline, and reacts to a rolled-over term only after the representative has told him about it.
The tool layer blocks nothing: confirm_partial_withdrawal_44cc2957 reads the certificate row, writes the
withdrawal entry, writes the penalty entry and updates the principal, with no status test, no error path and
no hint; it is callable and faithful while the certificate still stands in grace_period.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Write 1, subject cd_renew. Governing base policies: cd_rate_and_bonuses (subject cd_open, cd_renew) and
cd_evt_maturity_and_grace (subject cd_mature, cd_renew, cd_close, cd_deposit, cd_withdrawal). Neither carries
an eligibility gate that applies to cd_renew — cd_rate_and_bonuses declares none at all and
cd_evt_maturity_and_grace's grace_window applies to cd_deposit and cd_withdrawal — so both enter the contract
as policy_scope, and no time gate governs this write. The base clauses that keep force here are inherited in
full: the new term starts on the maturity date, the tier is the renewal target, the two bonuses stack by
simple addition, and the renewal rate basis is the target tier's published figures on the maturity date. What
is superseded is declared clause by clause in the policy's overwrite: the flat relationship bonus sentence,
the flat jumbo bonus sentence and the sentence measuring a renewal's principal after grace-period add-ons.
Write 2, subject cd_withdrawal. Governing base policies: cd_evt_early_withdrawal and cd_evt_maturity_and_grace.
Gates that apply to cd_withdrawal:
  active_only (state): "Principal can be withdrawn before maturity only from a certificate whose status is
  active." At the opening this is false — the certificate stands in grace_period — which is exactly the
  design; at the handling time of this write the renewal has landed and the status is active, evidenced by the
  delta of the preceding step. Object correlation: cd_certificates.certificate_id bound to the call's
  certificate_id.
  no_penalty_window (time): "A penalty-free withdrawal is allowed only after penalty_free_withdrawal_after_days
  calendar days have passed after the certificate was funded." The 12-Month Certificate publishes
  penalty_free_withdrawal_after_days as not_offered, so no day exists on which a withdrawal from this
  certificate becomes penalty-free and the gate bars nothing: the withdrawal is taken as a partial early
  withdrawal bearing the tier's penalty, which is what gold writes. Anchor: cd_certificates.term_start_date,
  relation not_before, counting the day after the term start as day 1, boundary exclusive. Boundary cases:
  just before — on any date at all, including 2026-06-11, the tier offers no penalty-free window, so a
  withdrawal cannot be classified penalty_free and must bear the penalty; at the boundary — there is no such
  boundary date on this tier, so the classification never changes and the penalty stands however long the
  certificate runs.
  grace_window (time, from cd_evt_maturity_and_grace): "Grace actions are allowed only while no more than
  grace_period_days calendar days have passed after the maturity date." At the handling time of this write the
  certificate's maturity date is 2027-05-28, so frozen_time 2026-06-12 is far inside "on or before maturity
  date plus ten days" and the gate is satisfied; it bars nothing because this withdrawal is not a grace
  action. Boundary cases: just before — 2027-06-07 would still be inside the window; at the boundary —
  2027-06-08 would be the first day past it, after which a withdrawal is again an early withdrawal of the new
  term, which is what this one already is.
  owner_confirms is retired by a declared overwrite: the extended policy replaces the two-step register-then-
  confirm sentence with the owner's own single in-person instruction, and the tool that carries it is
  owner=user, so the permission doctrine is kept and no pending instruction row is invented.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
Target object of both writes: the one certificate of deposit on this profile, certificate_number_last4 4417,
the row cd_certificates.<certificate>. The correlation key is certificate_id, carried by every ledger row read
and by both calls. Rows that enter the renewal computation: the 6500.00 deposit of 2026-06-02 with
deposit_kind grace_add_on (the only row posted after the maturity date) and nothing else from the ledger.
Rows that enter the penalty computation: the interest credit of 303.58 posted 2026-05-28 (the only interest
row inside the one month counted back from the day the principal leaves; the 336.15 credit of 2026-04-30
and every credit before it are excluded by the
window) and the two early partial withdrawals of 4000.00 and 3500.00, which the basis rule excludes here
because interest has been credited in that one month. Rows excluded and why: the twelve older interest
credits (outside that one month), the opening deposit of 101000.00 (a deposit of kind opening, not a
grace add-on), and the two penalty entries of 41.62 and 36.42 already booked against those withdrawals, which
are settled and are not re-charged. Each penalty entry carries source_item_id pointing at the withdrawal it
belongs to, so nothing on this ledger is offset against an object it is not linked to.

SEED: WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW EXISTS.
cd_certificates: the whole task. Remove the grace_period status or move the maturity date forward and the
prerequisite is satisfied at the opening and the tree collapses to one problem.
cd_transactions, opening deposit 101000.00 on 2025-05-28: fixes the term the ledger belongs to and, being at
or above the tier's jumbo threshold, explains why the term that ended carried both bonuses and a rate of 4.22.
cd_transactions, thirteen interest credits: the certificate compounds monthly, so the ledger looks like a real
year. The last of them, 303.58 on the maturity date, is the only one inside the one month counted back
from today and is what
the penalty basis is reduced by; the 2026-04-30 credit is the near miss — an agent who sums the term's
interest instead of the month's charges a basis of 99000-odd and writes a different penalty.
cd_transactions, two early partial withdrawals with their penalties: they are the near miss of the second
basis tier (had no interest been credited this month the basis would have been the sum removed together with
those 7500.00) and they are the evidence that the tier's two-partials-per-term allowance is counted over the
current term, which after the renewal begins on 2026-05-28 and holds none of them. Their penalties are booked
at the tier's published 90 days on the whole sum removed, which is what the standard method gives, and both
predate the money market account and the card, so no graded tier could have applied to them.
cd_transactions, grace add-on 6500.00 on 2026-06-02: without it the principal carried into the new term equals
the balance on record and the jumbo figure jumps from half points to full points, changing the rate to 4.19.
checking_accounts: the tier decides the relationship figure and the charged rate, the opening date of
2016-08-03 decides the charged rate's tier, the balance of 9240.55 decides the rounding of the penalty.
checking_transactions: five deposits inside the three-month window and two just outside it. The two outside,
2026-03-10 and 2026-02-27, are the near miss: counting them gives six and the full relationship points, and
the renewal rate comes out 4.17 rather than 4.14.
savings_accounts: 118600.00 in an active Premier Money Market. It carries the principal carried into the new
term over the jumbo threshold for the half-points tier, and it puts the penalty on the nine tenths tier.
card_accounts and card_transactions: the tier of the card decides the days charged, the 7341.60 of purchases
over twelve months decides the rounding of the assembled rate, and the three purchases in the last three
months decide the days tier. The 2500.00 payment and the 95.00 annual fee are in the ledger precisely because
they are not purchases.
No cache field is used as a trap in this task: the certificate's principal_balance is exactly the sum of its
ledger (101000.00 opened, 4132.63 of interest credited over thirteen credits, 7500.00 withdrawn, 78.04 of
penalties, 6500.00 added
in grace = 104054.59), so nothing in the world teaches an algorithm against the charter.
Automatic clauses checked row by row: the certificate compounds daily and credits monthly, which the thirteen
credits carry; the maturity has already happened and the grace window has already closed, which is the
state_due obligation this task discharges; no other automatic clause of the charter (funding lapse, dormancy,
bump-up window) is lit by any seeded row, and no seeded cross-category row lights an obligation in its own
difficulty — the checking, money market and card rows are ordinary posted activity in good standing.

FACTOR CARD — cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate (4 factors, result 4.14, whole baseline 4.22).
relationship_figure_grade (parameter, cross-difficulty checking): tiers are Premier or Private Client checking
with at least six deposits in three months / a qualifying checking tier with fewer than six / every other
owner, which is the fall-through the rule states as the complement of the two above. Evidence: checking_accounts variant_name Interest Checking, status active, and five checking_deposit
rows posted 2026-03-31, 2026-04-30, 2026-05-15, 2026-05-29, 2026-06-01. Tier taken: the middle one, three
quarters of 0.15 = 0.1125. Baseline reading (the computation document's flat "the tier's relationship bonus
points when the owner holds a qualifying account") gives 0.15 and a result of 4.17.
jumbo_figure_grade (parameter, cross-difficulty savings): tiers are carried principal at or above the jumbo
threshold with an active savings or money market account / carried principal below the threshold but at least
nine tenths of it and reaching the threshold together with that balance / neither. Evidence: carried principal
97554.59 and savings_accounts current_balance 118600.00, status active. Tier taken: the middle one, half of
0.10 = 0.05. Baseline reading gives 0 (97554.59 is below 100000.00) and a result of 4.09.
carried_principal_measure (method, this holding's ledger): tiers are a deposit posted after maturity on a
certificate whose ended term stood above the published rate / principal taken out after maturity with no
deposit posted / otherwise. Evidence: the 6500.00 grace add-on of 2026-06-02 and interest_rate 4.22 against
the tier's published 3.97. Tier taken: the first, so 104054.59 - 6500.00 = 97554.59. Baseline reading (the
balance standing on the certificate) gives 104054.59, which carries the jumbo figure to full points and a
result of 4.19.
assembled_rate_rounding (method, cross-difficulty card): tiers are card purchases over twelve months at or
above the higher spending figure / at or above the lower but below the higher / below the lower. Evidence:
7341.60 of card purchases posted between 2025-11-21 and 2026-06-04. Tier taken: the first, rounded up to the
next hundredth. Baseline reading (rounded down) gives 4.13.
Near miss for this computation: the two checking deposits just outside the three-month window.

FACTOR CARD — cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty (5 factors, result 687.42, whole baseline 1052.00).
penalty_basis_measure (method, this holding's ledger): tiers are interest credited in the one month counted
back from the day the principal leaves on
a certificate whose running rate stands above the published rate / principal taken out by an earlier partial
in the last twelve months with no interest credited this month / otherwise. Evidence: the 303.58 credit of
2026-05-28 and interest_rate 4.14 against 3.97. Tier taken: the first, so the basis is 103054.59 - 303.58 =
102751.01. Baseline reading (the sum the withdrawal removes) gives 103054.59 and a penalty of 689.45.
charged_rate_grade (parameter, cross-difficulty checking): tiers are a qualifying checking tier opened before
the term began / a non-qualifying tier opened before the term began / otherwise. Evidence: Interest Checking,
active, opened 2016-08-03, against term_start_date 2026-05-28. Tier taken: the first, 4.14 - 0.15 = 3.99.
Baseline reading (the rate the term carries) gives 4.14 and a penalty of 713.26.
charged_days_measure (method, cross-difficulty card): tiers are a Travel Rewards Visa Signature or Visa
Infinite Private Client with at least three purchases in three months / any other active card with at least
three / otherwise. Evidence: card_accounts variant_name Travel Rewards Visa Signature, status active, and
three card_purchase rows posted 2026-04-17, 2026-05-08 and 2026-06-04. Tier taken: the first, three quarters
of 90 rounded up to 68. Baseline reading (the tier's 90 published days) gives a penalty of 909.82.
charged_share_grade (parameter, cross-difficulty savings): tiers are a savings or money market balance at or
above the jumbo threshold with at least one earlier term / at least half the threshold but below it with at
least one earlier term / otherwise. Evidence: 118600.00 in the active money market and renewal_count 1 after
the renewal. Tier taken: the first, nine tenths. Baseline reading (the whole figure) gives 763.80.
charged_penalty_rounding (method, cross-difficulty checking): tiers are a checking balance at or above the
tier's smallest partial withdrawal with at least one earlier term / an active checking account below that
figure / otherwise. Evidence: ledger_balance 9240.55 against the tier's 500.00 minimum, and renewal_count 1.
Tier taken: the first, rounded up to the whole cent. Baseline reading (nearest cent, half up) gives 687.41.
Near miss for this computation: the twelve interest credits of the term that lie outside the one month
counted back from today, above all the 336.15 credited on 2026-04-30.

RULE AND COMPUTE, FORWARD AND BACK.
Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice carries a verbatim quotation in compute_basis —
balance_on_record and required_remaining quote the sentence fixing the largest sum a partial may remove;
grace_window_deposits, grace_window_withdrawals, bonus_points_on_ended_term and carried_principal quote the
measuring sentence; qualifying_checking_tier, checking_deposit_count and relationship_figure quote the
relationship grading sentence; savings_balance and jumbo_figure quote the jumbo grading sentence;
card_spend_twelve_months and rounded_rate quote the rounding sentence; on the penalty side
interest_credited_this_month, earlier_partial_principal, partials_taken_recently, bonus_points_carried and
charged_basis quote the basis grading sentence, checking_tier, checking_opened_before_term and applied_rate
the rate grading sentence, card_tier, card_purchase_count and charged_days the days grading sentence,
savings_balance and retained_share the share grading sentence, checking_balance and rounded_penalty the
rounding sentence.
Backward: every load-bearing sentence of both rules is claimed. "at or above the higher card spending figure"
-> the XSUM with within_months=12 and the K threshold; "in the three months before that day" -> the XCOUNT
with within_months=3; "in the one month counted back from the day the principal leaves" -> the SUM with
within_months=1; "rounded up to the next
hundredth" -> the int-plus-one construction; "rounded to the nearest cent with a half rounded up" -> the
int(x*100+0.5) construction; "rounded down to the hundredth" -> int(x*100)/100; "added together in that order
and the sum is rounded ... once, at the end" -> a single rounding binding over the assembled sum, not per
term; "the basis multiplied by the rate ... divided by one hundred, multiplied by the days ... and divided by
the tier's day count basis" -> raw_penalty in that order; "nine tenths of the figure" -> charged_penalty
applying the share to the raw figure before rounding, never after. No sentence is left without a binding and
no filter in the expressions is missing from the prose.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN.
The world was built, the renewal was replayed with the real task tool, and both computations were evaluated
with the skill's own restricted evaluator on the handling-time world. Output:
  cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate: result=4.14  (factor baselines 4.17 / 4.09 / 4.19 / 4.13; whole baseline 4.22)
  cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty: result=687.42  (factor baselines 689.45 / 713.26 / 909.82 / 763.80 /
  687.41; whole baseline 1052.00)
  penalty computed without the renewal write: 779.11 (the prerequisite sensitivity run)
Every factor moves the number, every whole baseline differs from gold, and the gold arguments are exactly
these figures. Intermediate bindings at handling time: carried_principal 97554.59, relationship_figure 0.1125,
jumbo_figure 0.05, assembled_rate 4.1325; charged_basis 102751.01, applied_rate 3.99, charged_days 68,
retained_share 0.9, raw_penalty 763.791891, charged_penalty 687.412702.

STANDARD SOLUTION.
Find the caller by his mobile number, verify him on three details, read the certificate, read its ledger, read
the checking account and its deposits, the money market balance, and the card and its purchases. Notice that
the certificate's maturity date has passed and its grace window closed while the status still reads
grace_period, and that the withdrawal rule waits on a certificate that carries the term now running. Assemble
the renewal rate: 3.97 published, plus 0.1125 relationship (a qualifying tier, five deposits in three months),
plus 0.05 jumbo (carried principal 97554.59 after setting aside the grace deposit, below the threshold but
above nine tenths of it and over the threshold with the money market balance), rounded up to 4.14 on twelve
months of card spending; the APY the same way to 4.22; the term 2026-05-28 to 2027-05-28 in the same tier.
Record the renewal. Then take the largest partial the rules allow, 104054.59 - 1000.00 = 103054.59, basis
103054.59 - 303.58 = 102751.01, rate 4.14 - 0.15 = 3.99, days three quarters of 90 rounded up to 68,
102751.01 x 3.99 / 100 x 68 / 365 = 763.791891, nine tenths of it 687.412702, rounded up to 687.42, paid by
official check, and hand the confirmation to the owner.

WHERE CARELESSNESS BITES.
Charging the penalty on the certificate as found (779.11). Counting the checking deposits over the whole
ledger rather than three months (4.17). Taking the balance on record as the principal carried into the new
term (4.19). Summing the term's interest instead of the month's for the basis. Counting the card payment or
the annual fee as purchases. Rounding the rate to the nearest hundredth instead of up (4.13), or the penalty
to the nearest cent instead of up (687.41). Each is excluded by a sentence of the published rules read against
the records, not by anything the caller says: he never corrects a figure.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT.
With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this worklog masked, and only the prose that will be
published, the tool schemas, what the lookups return and what the caller actually says: the withdrawal rule's
prerequisite sentence sends the reader to the certificate, whose maturity date and status show a term that
ended and a grace window that closed; the renewal rule fixes the tier, the dates and the assembled rate; the
grading paragraphs fix 0.1125, 0.05 and the rounding up; the withdrawal paragraphs fix 103054.59, 102751.01,
3.99, 68, nine tenths and rounding up. The draft lands on 4.14 and 687.42, the same as gold, and no second
reading of any sentence produces another pair — the one place two readings were possible, whether the sum
removed or the sum less credited interest is the basis, is settled outright by the grading sentence.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD.
Write 1 cites the certificate's status and maturity date as the system obligation that triggers it, its
renewal instruction as the discriminator, and declares both governing base policies as policy_scope because
neither has a gate applying to cd_renew. Write 2 cites the caller's own words as intent, "without closing it"
as the discriminator that separates a partial from a full withdrawal, the preceding renewal's delta as the
authority for the active status and the term dates, and frozen_time for both time gates. Every credential the
gold passes — 3365550312, 1958-03-14, 1327 — is stated verbatim by the caller, and no internal id is.
user_scenario:
Roland Whitacre is sixty-eight, a retired framing contractor who still keeps a chair in his son's shop off Battleground Avenue in Greensboro, and he calls the Piedmont Crescent Care Center mid-morning sounding brisk rather than worried. He and his wife are buying a smaller place out toward Asheboro, the closing is eight days off, and the bridge loan he was counting on fell through on Tuesday, so he needs cash out of the certificate of deposit he keeps at the bank. He says what he wants early and plainly: he wants to take as much as he can out of that certificate without closing it, because he is not willing to give up the whole term over one bad week, and he wants the money as an official check the bank mails to him, since his closing attorney asked for a bank check rather than a transfer. He mentions in passing that the certificate came due at the end of May and that he had meant to call about it then, but his wife's hip surgery got in the way.

He starts with his name, Roland Whitacre, and reads out his mobile number, 3365550312, as soon as the representative needs something to find him by. If he is asked to prove who he is he gives his date of birth, 1958-03-14, and then the last four digits of his Social Security number, 1327; if the representative still needs another detail he offers his ZIP code, 27408, or the email on the account, r.whitacre@pinebrookmail.com. When he is asked which certificate he means he can give the last four digits of the certificate number, 4417, and nothing beyond that: he tells the representative flatly that he has no reference numbers in front of him and that they will have to look the rest up on their side.

He does not know what the certificate is worth today and does not pretend to. Asked for a figure, he says it was right around a hundred thousand when he put it in, give or take, and that the bank's own record is the one to go by. He has no idea what taking money out early costs, he has no number of his own in mind, and he does not know how the bank works any of it out; if the representative quotes him a figure he takes it as read. He keeps a money market account and a checking account at the bank and a Visa he uses for travel, and he will say so if he is asked what else he has there, but he sees no reason any of that has to do with a certificate and does not bring it up himself.

He answers what he is asked and no more. If the representative tells him the certificate has rolled into a fresh term, or that the paperwork has it running again, he says that is news to him but he is not going to argue with the bank's records, and he waits. If he is told the sum he can take out and what will be charged for taking it, he says that will have to do and asks them to go ahead. When the representative hands the withdrawal over for him to carry out in person, he goes through with it there and then, reading back whatever the confirmation shows him. If he is asked to confirm that the proceeds should be a mailed official check rather than money moved into one of his own accounts, he says yes, the check, mailed to the address they have on file.

He never volunteers a step he has not been asked about, never suggests what the bank ought to do first, and never presses when a silence runs long. Once the withdrawal has actually been carried out and he has heard it confirmed, he thanks the representative, says the closing attorney will be glad to hear it, and rings off.

request_alignment.claim: The caller wants the largest sum his certificate of deposit will let him take out without closing it, paid to him as an official check.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.certificate_id: The certificate of deposit this customer holds, the one row the certificate lookup returns for this customer. Basis: the certificate lookup's own contract, 'Search by customer, certificate, or the account that receives its interest or proceeds', returns the single certificate standing on this profile. Uniqueness: the customer holds exactly one certificate, so no second certificate row can be meant, and the caller supplies the last four digits of the certificate number, 4417, which match that row.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_variant_name: 12-Month Certificate. Basis: the published rule for carrying a term over says 'The tier the certificate is carried into is the tier its own renewal target names', and the 12-Month Certificate names 12-Month Certificate as its renewal target. Uniqueness: the certificate stands in the 12-Month Certificate tier and its owner recorded no term change while the grace window was open, so none of the other five tier names can be reached from the records; the renewal instruction on the certificate reads auto_renew, which is the instruction that carries it into its renewal target rather than paying it out.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_term_start_date: 2026-05-28. Basis: 'The new term starts on the day the term that ended matured' and the certificate's maturity date on record is 2026-05-28. Uniqueness: the certificate carries exactly one maturity date, and the day the bank happens to record the renewal does not move the start of the term.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_maturity_date: 2027-05-28. Basis: the new term 'runs for the number of months the tier being renewed into publishes, so that its maturity falls that many calendar months after its start'. The 12-Month Certificate publishes a term of twelve months, and twelve calendar months after 2026-05-28 is 2027-05-28, a day that exists in that month so no month-end fall-back applies. Uniqueness: the term length is a published tier figure, not a choice.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_interest_rate: 4.14. The tier's published standard interest rate is 3.97. The relationship figure is graded: the owner's active checking account is an Interest Checking account, a tier the certificate's own tier lists as qualifying, and five deposits posted to it in the three months before today (2026-03-31, 2026-04-30, 2026-05-15, 2026-05-29 and 2026-06-01; the 2026-03-10 and 2026-02-27 deposits fall outside that window), which is fewer than six, so three quarters of the tier's 0.15 relationship bonus points are earned: 0.1125. The principal carried into the new term is measured as the balance standing on the certificate, 104054.59, less the deposit posted in the days after maturity, 6500.00 on 2026-06-02, because the rate of the term that ended, 4.22, stood above the tier's published 3.97: 97554.59. That figure is below the tier's jumbo threshold of 100000.00 but at least nine tenths of it, and together with the 118600.00 standing in the owner's active Premier Money Market account it passes the threshold, so half of the tier's 0.10 jumbo bonus points are earned: 0.05. Assembled: 3.97 + 0.1125 + 0.05 = 4.1325. The owner charged 7341.60 to the Travel Rewards Visa Signature in the twelve months before today, at or above the higher card spending figure of 6000.00, so the assembled rate is rounded up to the next hundredth: 4.14. Any agent reading the same records reaches the same figure.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_apy: 4.22. Basis: 'The annual percentage yield the new term carries is the tier's published standard annual percentage yield increased by the same relationship and jumbo figures and rounded the same way.' The 12-Month Certificate publishes a standard annual percentage yield of 4.05; the same 0.1125 relationship figure and 0.05 jumbo figure give 4.2125, and the same rounding up to the next hundredth gives 4.22. Uniqueness: the figures and the rounding are the ones already fixed for the rate, so no second reading is available.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.jumbo_bonus_applied: true. Basis: the tool's own contract, 'whether the rate written for the new term includes the jumbo bonus: true when the rate carries jumbo bonus points of any size'. Uniqueness: the rate written for the new term carries 0.05 of the tier's jumbo bonus points, which is points of some size, so false, the only other value, would misstate the rate that was written.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.relationship_bonus_applied: true. Basis: the same contract, 'true when the rate carries relationship bonus points of any size'. Uniqueness: the rate written carries 0.1125 relationship bonus points, so the only other value, false, would contradict the rate recorded on the same call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.certificate_id: The same certificate of deposit, identified by the certificate lookup for this customer. Basis: the certificate lookup returns one certificate for this profile, whose last four digits are 4417, matching what the caller states. Uniqueness: there is no second certificate on the profile, and the caller's own words, 'that certificate', point at the one he has just been read back.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.withdrawal_amount: 103054.59. Basis: 'The largest sum a single partial withdrawal may remove is the principal standing on the certificate less the balance the tier requires to remain after a partial withdrawal.' The principal standing on the certificate is 104054.59 and the 12-Month Certificate requires 1000.00 to remain, so the sum is 103054.59. Uniqueness: the caller asked for as much as he can take without closing the certificate, which the rule turns into exactly one figure; a larger sum would leave less than the tier requires and a smaller one would not be the largest.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.penalty_amount: 687.42. The basis is graded: interest of 303.58 was credited to the certificate on 2026-05-28, inside the one month counted back from today, and the rate of the term now running, 4.14, stands above the tier's published 3.97, so the basis is the sum removed less that credited interest: 103054.59 - 303.58 = 102751.01. The rate charged is graded: the owner holds an active Interest Checking account, a tier the certificate's own tier lists as qualifying, opened 2016-08-03, before the term now running began on 2026-05-28, so the rate is the rate the term carries less the tier's 0.15 relationship bonus points: 4.14 - 0.15 = 3.99. The days are graded: the owner holds an active Travel Rewards Visa Signature with three card purchases posted in the three months before today (2026-04-17, 2026-05-08 and 2026-06-04), at least three, so three quarters of the tier's 90 published penalty days, rounded up to a whole day, is 68. Together: 102751.01 x 3.99 / 100 x 68 / 365 = 763.7918913. The share charged is graded: the owner's active Premier Money Market balance of 118600.00 is at least the tier's jumbo threshold of 100000.00 and the certificate has run through one earlier term, so nine tenths of the figure is charged: 687.4127. The rounding is graded: the owner's active checking balance of 9240.55 is at least the 500.00 smallest partial withdrawal the tier accepts and the certificate has run through an earlier term, so the figure is rounded up to the whole cent: 687.42. Any agent reconciling the same ledger reaches the same figure.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.penalty_days: 68. Basis: 'an owner holding an active Travel Rewards Visa Signature or Visa Infinite Private Client card with at least three card purchases posted in the three months before the withdrawal is charged three quarters of the days the tier publishes, rounded up to a whole day'. The tier publishes 90 early withdrawal penalty days; three quarters of 90 is 67.5, rounded up to a whole day 68. Uniqueness: the card on the profile is a Travel Rewards Visa Signature in active status and three purchases posted to it inside the window, so neither the nine tenths tier nor the published-days tier can be reached, and the figure written on the entry is the figure the penalty was worked out with.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.rate_applied: 3.99. Basis: 'an owner holding an active checking account of a tier the certificate's own tier lists as qualifying, opened before the term now running began, is charged at the rate the term carries less the tier's relationship bonus points'. The rate the term carries is 4.14 and the tier's relationship bonus points are 0.15. Uniqueness: the Interest Checking account is in the certificate tier's qualifying list and was opened in 2016, long before the term now running began, so the published-standard-rate tier and the rate-as-carried tier are both excluded.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.destination: official_check. Basis: the caller's own instruction, 'he wants the money as an official check the bank mails to him, since his closing attorney asked for a bank check rather than a transfer', and the tool's contract, 'official_check applies when the bank draws an official check for the proceeds and mails it to the address on the owner's profile'. Uniqueness: checking and savings would move the proceeds into one of his own deposit accounts, which he has expressly declined, and none never holds for a withdrawal that pays money out.

edges.condition: The certificate's status is active and the term start date and maturity date it carries span the day of the withdrawal, so that the rate on the certificate is the rate of the term then running.
edges.policy_source: The penalty on principal taken out of a certificate before maturity is worked out only after the certificate carries the rate and the term dates of the term running on the day the principal leaves.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time 2026-06-12 the certificate still stands in grace_period carrying the term that ended: term_start_date 2025-05-28, maturity_date 2026-05-28 and interest_rate 4.22. The maturity date is fifteen days past and the tier's ten grace days ran out on 2026-06-07, so the dates and the rate on the certificate belong to no term that is running on the day the principal would leave, and there is no rate of the current term to charge a penalty at.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the renewal is recorded the certificate reads status active, term_start_date 2026-05-28, maturity_date 2027-05-28, interest_rate 4.14 and renewal_count 1, so the dates span 2026-06-12 and the rate is the rate of the term then running; the binding applied_rate moves from 4.07 to 3.99.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge and therefore a single topological order: the renewal is recorded, then the withdrawal is taken. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder, and the two writes do not commute — the penalty is read off the certificate the renewal rewrites, so taking the withdrawal first fixes it on the ended term's figures and on renewal_count 0 and leaves a different terminal state (penalty 779.11, principal 220.89 instead of 687.42 and 312.58).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the renewal write and replaying the rest unchanged gives penalty_amount 779.11 instead of 687.42: the charged rate falls back to 4.22 - 0.15 = 4.07 because the certificate still carries the ended term's rate, and the share charged rises from nine tenths to the whole figure because renewal_count is still 0. The certificate's terminal principal_balance changes with it, and the certificate is left in grace_period with no new term on record.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names the renewal problem, the thing it resolves or anything that would steer the agent to it: the words renewal, roll over, new term, grace and term change do not appear as anything the caller raises, and he never asks whether something has to be sorted out first. He says only that the certificate 'came due at the end of May' as his own timeline for why he is calling now, which the record independently carries as maturity_date 2026-05-28. His one reaction touching the prerequisite is passive and conditional: only if the representative tells him the certificate has rolled into a fresh term does he say that is news to him and wait. If the representative never discovers it he neither reminds nor presses, and the consequence falls on the scoring alone.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_partial_withdrawal_44cc2957 in task_tools.py looks the certificate row up only to copy its customer and its principal, then creates the withdrawal entry, creates the penalty entry and updates the principal. It tests no status, no term date and no rate, has no branch that can refuse, returns no error path and gives no hint; called while the certificate still stands in grace_period it writes exactly as faithfully, and the only trace of the missing renewal is a different terminal hash.

factor_trace: relationship_figure_grade (parameter): the active checking account is an Interest Checking account, a tier the 12-Month Certificate lists as qualifying, and five checking deposits posted inside the three months before 2026-06-12 (2026-03-31, 2026-04-30, 2026-05-15, 2026-05-29, 2026-06-01), fewer than six, so the middle tier applies and selects three quarters of the tier's 0.15 relationship bonus points, 0.1125; the computation document's default, the tier's relationship bonus points in full, would have given 0.15 and a rate of 4.17.

jumbo_figure_grade (parameter): the principal carried into the new term is 97554.59, below the tier's 100000.00 jumbo threshold but above nine tenths of it, and the owner's active Premier Money Market balance of 118600.00 carries the two together past the threshold, so the middle tier applies and selects half of the tier's 0.10 jumbo bonus points, 0.05; the default, the tier's jumbo bonus points only at or above the threshold, would have given 0 and a rate of 4.09.

carried_principal_measure (method): the ledger carries a 6500.00 deposit posted 2026-06-02, after the maturity date of 2026-05-28, and the ended term's rate of 4.22 stands above the tier's published 3.97, so the first tier applies and the principal carried in is measured as 104054.59 less that deposit, 97554.59; the standard method, the balance standing on the certificate, would have given 104054.59, which carries the jumbo figure to full points and the rate to 4.19.

assembled_rate_rounding (method): card purchases of 7341.60 posted to the Travel Rewards Visa Signature between 2025-11-21 and 2026-06-04 are at or above the higher card spending figure of 6000.00, so the first tier applies and the assembled 4.1325 is rounded up to the next hundredth, 4.14; the standard method, rounded down to the hundredth, would have given 4.13.
balance_on_record (no factor): a plain read of principal_balance, 104054.59.
grace_window_withdrawals (no factor, evidence of the carried-principal tiers): 0.00, since no principal was taken out after maturity.
assembled_rate (no factor): plumbing, 3.97 + 0.1125 + 0.05 = 4.1325, the published starting point and the two figures added in that order.
